clusters.state_of_play: Russia has suspended shipping in the Sea of Azov after Ukraine targeted 90 vessels, including shadow fleet oil tankers, in under a week. Ukraine also released video of strikes on 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea, including 17 oil tankers. Ukraine's drone forces chief Robert Brovdi confirmed overnight strikes on 10 tankers, 4 ferries, and Russia's Syzran refinery in the Samara region. The attacks have triggered a nationwide fuel shortage in Russia, with queues reported at fuel stations and Russia now seeking gasoline imports from India in a reversal of trade flow. These strikes fall under a formal 40-day campaign Zelenskyy announced on 26 June, ordering Ukraine's state security service to target Russian territory to compel an end to the war. Russia has struck back: a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv and further strikes across Ukraine have killed at least 16 people over two days. Mayor Vitali Klitschko previously reported emergency services battling fires across the capital following an earlier missile strike. Ukraine is also targeting Crimea as part of a strategy to demonstrate Putin's failure to defend the peninsula. On POW executions, a Ukrainian intelligence official told AFP that more than 900 military personnel have been killed in more than 340 incidents since 2022. The UN reported June was the deadliest month for Ukrainian civilians since April 2022, with 293 killed and 1,990 wounded, bringing total verified civilian deaths to 16,431 since February 2022. Inside Ukraine, President Zelenskyy's dismissal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has triggered rare wartime protests across the country, with thousands of soldiers, veterans, and civilians demanding his reappointment; the deputy air force commander has also resigned in protest. Parliament has now approved Koretskyi as the new Prime Minister, following PM Yulia Svyrydenko's resignation. The EU and Ukraine signed a drone deal to boost joint production and establish joint ventures; Brussels has also allowed Kyiv to use part of a €6bn EU tranche to buy Chinese drone parts that are in short supply in Europe. The EU separately failed to agree its latest round of sanctions against Russia. UK PM Keir Starmer travelled to Kyiv to meet Zelenskyy, reaffirming UK support, in what is described as a farewell trip before he hands over to Andy Burnham. On the Coalition of the Willing, Bulgaria's PM Rumen Radev has withdrawn Bulgaria from the group, and Ukrainian politician Kira Rudik has warned that upcoming European national elections could produce a very different coalition next year. Separately, Poland-Ukraine relations face strain over Kyiv's decision to honour WWII fighters responsible for killing roughly 100,000 Poles.

clusters.state_of_play: France's lower house of parliament has adopted an assisted dying law for terminally ill patients by 291 votes to 241, bypassing the right-wing dominated Senate. The law now goes to France's highest constitutional court for approval before it can take effect. The legislation fulfills a campaign promise made by President Macron when re-elected in 2022, and would make France the latest country to guarantee the right to assisted dying, joining the Netherlands, Belgium, Switzerland, and Canada. Separately, France's national soccer team has been eliminated from the World Cup after a 2-0 semi-final defeat to Spain in Dallas, ending Didier Deschamps' managerial tenure; his final game will be Saturday's third-place play-off. Zinedine Zidane is closing in on appointment as his successor amid public criticism from Kylian Mbappe. Hours after the semi-final, Spain and Barcelona star Lamine Yamal's £9.5m Barcelona mansion — formerly owned by Gerard Pique and Shakira — was targeted by burglars, with police opening an investigation.

clusters.state_of_play: Russia has suspended shipping in the Sea of Azov after Ukraine targeted 90 vessels, including shadow fleet oil tankers, in under a week. Ukraine also released video of strikes on 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea, including 17 oil tankers. Ukraine's drone forces chief Robert Brovdi confirmed overnight strikes on 10 tankers, 4 ferries, and Russia's Syzran refinery in the Samara region. The attacks have triggered a nationwide fuel shortage in Russia, with queues reported at fuel stations and Russia now seeking gasoline imports from India in a reversal of trade flow. These strikes fall under a formal 40-day campaign Zelenskyy announced on 26 June, ordering Ukraine's state security service to target Russian territory to compel an end to the war. Russia has struck back: a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv and further strikes across Ukraine have killed at least 16 people over two days. Mayor Vitali Klitschko previously reported emergency services battling fires across the capital following an earlier missile strike. Ukraine is also targeting Crimea as part of a strategy to demonstrate Putin's failure to defend the peninsula. On POW executions, a Ukrainian intelligence official told AFP that more than 900 military personnel have been killed in more than 340 incidents since 2022. The UN reported June was the deadliest month for Ukrainian civilians since April 2022, with 293 killed and 1,990 wounded, bringing total verified civilian deaths to 16,431 since February 2022. Inside Ukraine, President Zelenskyy's dismissal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has triggered rare wartime protests across the country, with thousands of soldiers, veterans, and civilians demanding his reappointment; the deputy air force commander has also resigned in protest. Parliament has now approved Koretskyi as the new Prime Minister, following PM Yulia Svyrydenko's resignation. The EU and Ukraine signed a drone deal to boost joint production and establish joint ventures; Brussels has also allowed Kyiv to use part of a €6bn EU tranche to buy Chinese drone parts that are in short supply in Europe. The EU separately failed to agree its latest round of sanctions against Russia. UK PM Keir Starmer travelled to Kyiv to meet Zelenskyy, reaffirming UK support, in what is described as a farewell trip before he hands over to Andy Burnham. On the Coalition of the Willing, Bulgaria's PM Rumen Radev has withdrawn Bulgaria from the group, and Ukrainian politician Kira Rudik has warned that upcoming European national elections could produce a very different coalition next year. Separately, Poland-Ukraine relations face strain over Kyiv's decision to honour WWII fighters responsible for killing roughly 100,000 Poles.

clusters.state_of_play: The US cyclosporiasis outbreak continues to worsen, with cases now reported across 40 states and more than 5,500 confirmed; CDC's tally of confirmed or under-investigation cases stands at nearly 7,000, with 1,645 lab-confirmed. Michigan alone now accounts for 3,300+ cases, with officials pointing to lettuce or salad greens as a likely source. CDC has identified a link among four Midwestern states and expects the outbreaks to continue through August. Taco Bell has pulled implicated ingredients. RFK Jr. faces scrutiny over CDC's response, and cyclospora was dropped from the federal monitoring program last summer. Funding cuts are also hampering CDC's ability to track the outbreak, with no source yet confirmed. On Wednesday, Trump's CDC director nominee Erica Schwartz faced Senate confirmation, vowing to 'never betray the science' and pledge 'radical transparency,' but struggled to convince senators she would stand up to RFK Jr. Separately, Trump's health emergency preparedness nominee Sean Kaufman walked back past comments skeptical of Covid-19 and hepatitis B vaccine safety, drawing a heated exchange with Sen. Cassidy. Separately, a new Legionnaires' disease outbreak has emerged on Manhattan's Upper East Side with 60 cases; the source remains unclear. The DRC Ebola outbreak — now the fastest-growing in history, killing roughly 100 per week — continues to worsen. Confirmed cases have reached 2,011 with 754 deaths; WHO warns the true count may be 2–4 times larger. Critically, 80% of new cases are now emerging from unknown transmission chains, meaning the outbreak is spreading faster than it can be tracked. The outbreak has spread to additional DRC provinces. Maternal mortality has doubled in the outbreak zone, with an estimated 63,000 pregnant women at risk as mothers avoid hospitals. WHO has launched the first clinical trial of an antiviral drug to prevent Bundibugyo strain Ebola infection, and Oxford University has begun human trials of a new Ebola vaccine in the UK. Healthcare workers at a DRC Ebola treatment centre remain on strike over unpaid salaries, and health workers in Ituri province have separately begun striking over unpaid wages. A second US national has been evacuated to Germany for treatment, and the Trump administration is barring Americans in the DRC from returning to the US on commercial flights. CDC travel restrictions have been extended to also cover some travelers from Uganda and South Sudan. The Ebola outbreak also threatens to cancel a UK-backed kidney transplant programme in Uganda. Separately, UK health officials are warning of a rapid rise in imported Zika virus cases, and Los Angeles County has reported its first West Nile virus case of 2026.

clusters.state_of_play: Russia has suspended shipping in the Sea of Azov after Ukraine targeted 90 vessels, including shadow fleet oil tankers, in under a week. Ukraine also released video of strikes on 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea, including 17 oil tankers. Ukraine's drone forces chief Robert Brovdi confirmed overnight strikes on 10 tankers, 4 ferries, and Russia's Syzran refinery in the Samara region. The attacks have triggered a nationwide fuel shortage in Russia, with queues reported at fuel stations and Russia now seeking gasoline imports from India in a reversal of trade flow. These strikes fall under a formal 40-day campaign Zelenskyy announced on 26 June, ordering Ukraine's state security service to target Russian territory to compel an end to the war. Russia has struck back: a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv and further strikes across Ukraine have killed at least 16 people over two days. Mayor Vitali Klitschko previously reported emergency services battling fires across the capital following an earlier missile strike. Ukraine is also targeting Crimea as part of a strategy to demonstrate Putin's failure to defend the peninsula. On POW executions, a Ukrainian intelligence official told AFP that more than 900 military personnel have been killed in more than 340 incidents since 2022. The UN reported June was the deadliest month for Ukrainian civilians since April 2022, with 293 killed and 1,990 wounded, bringing total verified civilian deaths to 16,431 since February 2022. Inside Ukraine, President Zelenskyy's dismissal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has triggered rare wartime protests across the country, with thousands of soldiers, veterans, and civilians demanding his reappointment; the deputy air force commander has also resigned in protest. Parliament has now approved Koretskyi as the new Prime Minister, following PM Yulia Svyrydenko's resignation. The EU and Ukraine signed a drone deal to boost joint production and establish joint ventures; Brussels has also allowed Kyiv to use part of a €6bn EU tranche to buy Chinese drone parts that are in short supply in Europe. The EU separately failed to agree its latest round of sanctions against Russia. UK PM Keir Starmer travelled to Kyiv to meet Zelenskyy, reaffirming UK support, in what is described as a farewell trip before he hands over to Andy Burnham. On the Coalition of the Willing, Bulgaria's PM Rumen Radev has withdrawn Bulgaria from the group, and Ukrainian politician Kira Rudik has warned that upcoming European national elections could produce a very different coalition next year. Separately, Poland-Ukraine relations face strain over Kyiv's decision to honour WWII fighters responsible for killing roughly 100,000 Poles.

clusters.state_of_play: The two Fontainebleau forest fires, which have burned just over 2,000 hectares south of Paris since Sunday, have been declared 'contained' by local Prefect Pierre Ory on Tuesday evening, though they are not yet extinguished. Around 950 firefighters supported by aerial teams remain on scene and are expected to stay for days if not weeks. Five people have been arrested on suspicion of deliberately starting the fires, including a volunteer firefighter who admitted to setting fire to twigs using matches and gasoline; a second suspect admitted to accidentally starting a fire by discarding a cigarette. Investigators had previously found ten ignition points near the origin. Around 1,000 people were evacuated. French President Emmanuel Macron is due to visit the site. Officials described the blaze as of 'exceptional scale', with road and rail links disrupted. The fire coincides with France's third heatwave since May, which forced early closures of the Eiffel Tower, Louvre, and Musée d'Orsay, and led many towns to cancel Bastille Day fireworks displays.

These strikes fall under a formal 40-day campaign Zelenskyy announced on 26 June, ordering Ukraine's state security service to target Russian territory to compel an end to the war. Russia has struck back: a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv and further strikes across Ukraine have killed at least 16 people over two days. Mayor Vitali Klitschko previously reported emergency services battling fires across the capital following an earlier missile strike. Ukraine is also targeting Crimea as part of a strategy to demonstrate Putin's failure to defend the peninsula. On POW executions, a Ukrainian intelligence official told AFP that more than 900 military personnel have been killed in more than 340 incidents since 2022. The UN reported June was the deadliest month for Ukrainian civilians since April 2022, with 293 killed and 1,990 wounded, bringing total verified civilian deaths to 16,431 since February 2022. Inside Ukraine, President Zelenskyy's dismissal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has triggered rare wartime protests across the country, with thousands of soldiers, veterans, and civilians demanding his reappointment; the deputy air force commander has also resigned in protest. Parliament has now approved Koretskyi as the new Prime Minister, following PM Yulia Svyrydenko's resignation. The EU and Ukraine signed a drone deal to boost joint production and establish joint ventures; Brussels has also allowed Kyiv to use part of a €6bn EU tranche to buy Chinese drone parts that are in short supply in Europe. The EU separately failed to agree its latest round of sanctions against Russia. UK PM Keir Starmer travelled to Kyiv to meet Zelenskyy, reaffirming UK support, in what is described as a farewell trip before he hands over to Andy Burnham. On the Coalition of the Willing, Bulgaria's PM Rumen Radev has withdrawn Bulgaria from the group, and Ukrainian politician Kira Rudik has warned that upcoming European national elections could produce a very different coalition next year. Separately, Poland-Ukraine relations face strain over Kyiv's decision to honour WWII fighters responsible for killing roughly 100,000 Poles.

clusters.state_of_play: New York Governor Kathy Hochul has signed an executive order imposing the first statewide moratorium on new large (hyperscaler) data centers for one year, citing energy grid, environmental, and ratepayer cost concerns, including ensuring New Yorkers do not bear costs of transmission and infrastructure build-outs, while state lawmakers draft a nation-leading regulatory framework. The moratorium is drawing backlash from critics who say it will further damage upstate New York's already sagging economy. President Trump has publicly blasted the moratorium, demanding Hochul reverse the policy immediately. The action follows a growing left-wing grassroots campaign, backed by Sanders-aligned progressives, opposing AI data center expansion. Similar grassroots opposition is emerging elsewhere, including Paulding County, Georgia, where furious homeowners packed standing-room-only county commission meetings and held a protest demanding a local moratorium, and in Florida, where residents near a proposed hyperscale data center in Trump's backyard are fuming over water supply risks despite the project's claim of generating over $500 million in annual tax revenue. Opposition to AI data centers is emerging as one of the rare cross-partisan political issues of the cycle. Separately, a PJM power auction covering the nation's largest electrical grid is projected to add $6.3 billion in additional charges to consumers and businesses across 13 states as a direct result of data center electricity demand. Axios has framed Hochul's moratorium as a replicable Democratic playbook for other governors ahead of the 2026 midterms. The backlash against AI data centers is now global in scope: India is fast-tracking hyperscale data center megaprojects to catch up technologically, but critics warn coastal cities face energy and water depletion with few long-term jobs created. Australia is moving to impose energy and water guardrails on data centers amid the AI boom and also seeks to protect the rights of creators whose work is used to train AI models; Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's Labor government is additionally developing a new national AI framework to address the technology's growing economic and social impacts.

US strikes have hit port cities of Bushehr and Bandar Abbas, as well as a 90-minute attack on Iran's Greater Tunb Island targeting cruise missile storage and launch sites. US attacks have killed dozens in Iran, pushing a fragile ceasefire closer to collapse. A Situation Room meeting was held to plan a wider offensive broader in scope than the current Strait of Hormuz campaign. Trump warned strikes would intensify next week if Iran does not cooperate in peace talks, while also calling off a previously announced 20% fee on Hormuz shipping, replacing it with investment and trade deals with Gulf Arab states. US strikes hit an Iranian army barracks, killing at least 7 troops and wounding more than 260 people across the country. Iran has threatened to halt all Middle East energy exports in response to the blockade. Iran claims to have destroyed the US Fifth Fleet command centre and targeted a US naval support base in Bahrain's capital, with sirens reported in Manama. Iran has also attacked Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan; Jordan shot down three Iranian missiles. Iran claims to have killed 3 US service members in Kuwait, while the official US death toll stands at 14. The US used sea drones in combat for the first time to strike an Iranian submarine and ship maintenance facility near the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude is above $87 per barrel. Dubai has announced plans to build a new port to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, and Gulf states more broadly are exploring alternative routes. Former officials say a stable peace appears elusive and characterise the current Hormuz campaign as Trump's third major strategic shift in the Iran conflict. Separately, Ukraine has struck more than 100 Russian vessels in the Sea of Azov over nine days and has also struck 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea, including 17 oil tankers. Russia's Agriculture Ministry is actively seeking alternative shipping routes and denies the strikes will affect export capacity, though Russian oil at sea is near a year-high as Moscow struggles to sell its exports. Russian strikes on Odesa killed at least 3 people and wounded 3 others. Trump has said Putin is ready to make a deal to end the Ukraine war, though Russia has warned that Western troops enforcing any ceasefire would be treated as military targets. The EU and Ukraine have signed a drone deal to boost joint production and establish joint ventures, combining Ukraine's battlefield expertise with EU scale. Treasury Secretary Bessent has announced a Trump gold coin featuring the sitting president will go into production. In China, official data shows GDP grew 4.3% in Q2, the weakest quarterly growth since late 2022, driven by slow consumer demand despite a surge in exports. DeepSeek is weighing an IPO and considering raising new private funds after completing a first financing round that valued the company at $52 billion; Zhipu has separately embraced an AGI positioning. Hong Kong police raided two bookstores and arrested five people for allegedly selling seditious publications, underscoring the political changes that have eroded the territory's once-open publishing environment.

Biddeford, Maine mayor Liam LaFountain has also commented publicly on the incident.

clusters.state_of_play: Russia has suspended shipping in the Sea of Azov after Ukraine targeted 90 vessels, including shadow fleet oil tankers, in under a week. Ukraine also released video of strikes on 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea, including 17 oil tankers. Ukraine's drone forces chief Robert Brovdi confirmed overnight strikes on 10 tankers, 4 ferries, and Russia's Syzran refinery in the Samara region. The attacks have triggered a nationwide fuel shortage in Russia, with queues reported at fuel stations and Russia now seeking gasoline imports from India in a reversal of trade flow. These strikes fall under a formal 40-day campaign Zelenskyy announced on 26 June, ordering Ukraine's state security service to target Russian territory to compel an end to the war. Russia has struck back: a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv and further strikes across Ukraine have killed at least 16 people over two days. Mayor Vitali Klitschko previously reported emergency services battling fires across the capital following an earlier missile strike. Ukraine is also targeting Crimea as part of a strategy to demonstrate Putin's failure to defend the peninsula. On POW executions, a Ukrainian intelligence official told AFP that more than 900 military personnel have been killed in more than 340 incidents since 2022. The UN reported June was the deadliest month for Ukrainian civilians since April 2022, with 293 killed and 1,990 wounded, bringing total verified civilian deaths to 16,431 since February 2022. Inside Ukraine, President Zelenskyy's dismissal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has triggered rare wartime protests across the country, with thousands of soldiers, veterans, and civilians demanding his reappointment; the deputy air force commander has also resigned in protest. Parliament has now approved Koretskyi as the new Prime Minister, following PM Yulia Svyrydenko's resignation. The EU and Ukraine signed a drone deal to boost joint production and establish joint ventures; Brussels has also allowed Kyiv to use part of a €6bn EU tranche to buy Chinese drone parts that are in short supply in Europe. The EU separately failed to agree its latest round of sanctions against Russia. UK PM Keir Starmer travelled to Kyiv to meet Zelenskyy, reaffirming UK support, in what is described as a farewell trip before he hands over to Andy Burnham. On the Coalition of the Willing, Bulgaria's PM Rumen Radev has withdrawn Bulgaria from the group, and Ukrainian politician Kira Rudik has warned that upcoming European national elections could produce a very different coalition next year. Separately, Poland-Ukraine relations face strain over Kyiv's decision to honour WWII fighters responsible for killing roughly 100,000 Poles.

The new exhibit drew criticism from advocates and Philadelphia Mayor Cherelle L. Parker, who said the removal happened under cover of darkness. Critics argue the new panels present a sanitized view of US history. Separately, a $69 million NPS exhibit beneath the Lincoln Memorial, opened less than a month ago, is reported to be endangering rare 1860s copies of the Emancipation Proclamation and Thirteenth Amendment due to defective light screens and unsafe temperatures, according to NPS staff. In an unrelated Philadelphia incident, Vietnam veteran George Barr, 75, has been charged with the murder of Silas Hanrahan, 21, a British illegal immigrant and alleged member of a traveler conman gang, who was shot dead at Barr's home; neighbors have made disturbing allegations about Hanrahan's conduct prior to the shooting. Also unrelated: a British pub landlady, 65, was shot dead in front of her husband during a Caribbean holiday. The Caricom Reparations Commission, visiting the UK, has called for the return of the British Virgin Islands and for King Charles to commit to decolonising Britain's remaining overseas territories.
